title: AI dropped the cost of writing to zero. In return, it made reading the most expensive bottleneck in your company.
sources: Harvard Business Review on The Asymmetry of AI Content Generation and Workplace Reading Burden 2026
Computerworld and ACM Research on Attention Tax and AI Comprehension Debt 2026
text: Generating text with AI is practically free. Reading it is quietly bankrupting your team. Two years ago, a team lead had to think clearly and condense an update into four crisp sentences. Today, anyone can type four words into a prompt box: "Write a comprehensive project update." Ten seconds later, an algorithm spits out 1,200 words of corporate text. It looks polished. It has bullet points, headers, and buzzwords. And then they hit send. Now eight colleagues receive that update. Each person spends 15 minutes wading through synthetic fluff just to find the two decisions that actually affect their week. The sender saved two minutes. The team collectively burned two hours. Welcome to Draft Inflation: the defining workplace exhaustion of 2026. When the cost of producing text dropped to zero, the volume of words exploded. But human cognitive bandwidth stayed the same. Workers now spend half their workday paying an uncredited Attention Tax. You are not creating value. You are panning for gold in an endless river of machine generated filler. Management usually offers the worst possible fix: "Just use AI to summarize it." So employee A uses a chatbot to blow three points up into 1,000 words. Employee B uses another chatbot to shrink those 1,000 words back into three bullet points. Two models talking to each other through two exhausted humans clicking copy and paste. The orchestrator shift: High leverage teams in 2026 do not buy another chatbot subscription and tell staff to read faster. They eliminate text bloat by replacing chat boxes with deterministic background orchestration: 1. Strict Schema Contracts Operational updates are captured through structured fields. If an update does not fit four clean parameters (Status, Root Blocker, Metric Delta, Next Action), the pipeline halts. No more unconstrained corporate essays. 2. Direct System Ingestion Project metrics and blockers are pulled directly from databases and issue trackers via read only webhooks. Context is retrieved deterministically before any summary exists, eliminating hallucinated claims. 3. Decision Cards Instead of Reading Memos Operators never read an eight page brief for routine workflows. The engine synthesizes the delta, runs policy checks, and presents a single card: Approve or Reject, with the raw data diff attached. Stop celebrating how many words your employees produce with AI. Start measuring how much useless reading your systems eliminate. Real automation is not about faster typing. It is about removing noise so people can make decisions. How many pages of AI generated updates did you have to read through this week? #EnterpriseAI #WorkflowAutomation #Productivity #FutureOfWork #Operations
